outcome.technical: _locks.pid_alive (plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_locks.py:150-183) keeps os.kill(pid,0) as the first question and, when it succeeds or raises PermissionError, asks a second: pid==os.getpid() is alive, otherwise not _is_zombie(pid). New _is_zombie (_locks.py:185-209) reads /proc/<pid>/stat (state letter after the last ')') where it exists, else `ps -o stat= -p <pid>` (10 s timeout, utf-8/replace); anything unreadable is not-a-zombie, i.e. stays 'present' as before. Windows branch untouched (no zombie state; pl1 is its case). Probed on this macOS (Darwin 25.6.0, arm64): a SIGKILLed, unreaped child -> os.kill(pid,0) succeeds, `ps -o stat=` prints 'Z', /proc absent, os.waitpid(1, WNOHANG) on a non-child raises ChildProcessError(ECHILD) so waitpid is no answer for a pid not owned; after the parent reaps, os.kill raises ProcessLookupError. Linux not probed: reasoned from proc(5) (state Z in field 3 of /proc/<pid>/stat) and kill(2) (succeeds for a zombie). SECOND CHANGE, caused by the first and found by the full sweep: test_close_phase lk6/lk7 went red intermittently (e.g. 3 of 6 runs; HEAD export 0 of 6) with 'index looks abandoned ... pid N is gone'. Cause: acquire reads a held claim then judges its holder; a holder that releases and exits in between used to read ALIVE for as long as it stayed an unreaped zombie, which masked an existing read-then-judge window; with zombies now gone the window shows. acquire (_locks.py ~1268-1276) now re-asks the name when the holder is judged dead but the claim judged is no longer the file on disk (stamp None or changed) instead of refusing E_STALE; a claim still standing is refused as before. After the fix test_close_phase 269/269 on 6 consecutive runs. THIRD: an encoding lint (test__output en5) flagged the new open()/subprocess.run() without encoding; both now name encoding=utf-8, errors=replace. FOURTH, test_run_test_gate.py (outside `files`; the plan gate allowed the Edit): the liveness case asserted product_says_alive is True for the zombie solo child (the defect pinned as expected); changed to `is False` (line 8210) because the case's own title already says a zombie counts as gone on the product's liveness rule. NOT DONE: tests/_harness.py (comment at ~1099-1104 says the product rule 'counts it ALIVE ... the product rule is left as it is', now false, and _harness._is_zombie/_pid_present duplicate the new rule) - the Edit was refused verbatim: '[require-plan] plugins/audit/tests/_harness.py is outside task P128.33-0h5, the task this worktree is bound to ... it is declared by P72.1, P92.1, ... a different task. Only that task's files are open here.' A follow-up should reduce _pid_present to `_locks.pid_alive(pid) is not False`, delete harness _is_zombie and rewrite that comment; _group_present keeps its own ps walk (no product rule for groups). Requirement clause: 'Register F693. _locks.pid_alive is os.kill(pid, 0), true for a zombie; callers asking about pids they do not own read a dead process as alive until reaped.' -> DONE at _locks.py:150-209, case at plugins/audit/tests/test__locks.py (block headed 'an exited process nobody has reaped yet reads dead'), callers (_proc_group._gone, stamp-verification, panel-server, tools/_suite, audit-lock) all go through pid_alive so none needed a change. Added cases: the tests.add clause verbatim; pz0 (fixture is a Z-state zombie that kill(pid,0) still accepts, read from the process table by test-side _table_state, not by the code under test), pz1 (reaped pid still False), pz2/pz3 (let-go-between-read-and-judge retried; still-standing claim still E_STALE). Helper _bare_signal_sees is module-level because test_run_test_gate forbids a signal-0 read after a kill in one function. Falsifier for pz3's over-fire direction (unconditional continue) would hang rather than fail; not separately mutated.
